title: Electric Service Agreement: Agreements per Customer and per Service Address
content:
**Customer Care Center desk guidance: how many Electric Service Agreements a customer holds, and what one service address allows**

The desk applies the following rule to every start of an Electric Service Agreement with Lakeshore Power & Light Company.

## The rule the desk applies

1. **Number per customer.** A customer may hold any number of Electric Service Agreements, one for each service address the customer occupies or operates; there is no cap on the number per customer.
2. **One open agreement per address.** A new start is opened only when no other Electric Service Agreement at the same service address is in pending start, active, notice pending or disconnected status. The test is made on the company's own agreement records before the start is opened, matching agreements by the service address as recorded on the start order; the customer's statement does not decide it.
3. **An agreement still open in another customer's name.** When an agreement at the address is still open in another customer's name, the new start is not opened until that agreement is closed, either by its own holder's stop-service order or by its closure after disconnection. A care center agent never closes another customer's agreement.
4. **Independence of addresses.** Agreements of the same customer at different service addresses are independent of one another for billing, for notices and for disconnection.

## Status of the other agreement at the same address

| Other agreement at the same service address | New start at that address |
|---|---|
| none on record | may be opened |
| pending start | not opened |
| active | not opened |
| notice pending | not opened |
| disconnected | not opened |
| closed | does not stand in the way |

## Points of judgement (hypothetical cases)

- *Hypothetical:* a customer already holds two active agreements at two different addresses and asks to start service at a third address where every earlier agreement is closed. The number of agreements the customer already holds does not stand in the way, and the closed agreements at the third address do not either.
- *Hypothetical:* the agreement at the requested address is disconnected and still in a former occupant's name. It is still open under the rule above, so the new start is not opened until that agreement is closed by its holder's stop-service order or by closure after disconnection.
- *Hypothetical:* one of the customer's agreements carries a pending disconnection notice. Its notice status has no bearing on the customer's agreements at other addresses.
